## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The Ollama launch blog recommends glm-4.7-flash (about 23 GB VRAM at 64k context), qwen3-coder and gpt-oss:20b locally, and cloud models such as glm-4.7:cloud, minimax-m2.1:cloud, gpt-oss:120b-cloud and qwen3-coder:480b-cloud. Later docs examples name newer models, so model recommendations date quickly. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-23) — https://ollama.com/blog/launch · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] OpenCode manual setup uses `opencode.json` with provider id ollama, npm package @ai-sdk/openai-compatible, options.baseURL http://localhost:11434/v1 and a models map. OpenCode's docs say Ollama can auto-configure OpenCode (pointing to the Ollama integration page) and advise, if tool calls fail, raising Ollama's `num_ctx` (start around 16k-32k). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/ · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI · also: https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/opencode
- [statement] Context length: Ollama's blog and integration pages advise at least 64k tokens for coding agents; GitHub advises at least 128k for Copilot CLI BYOK; OpenCode's docs treat `num_ctx` (16k-32k start) as the first fix when tool calls fail. Ollama's default context is too small for these agents, so raise it before launching. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://ollama.com/blog/launch · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI · also: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/use-byok-models, https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/
- [statement] Negation: a hands-on test (Ollama v0.15.1, Claude Code v2.1.15, M4 32GB) found small local models impractical with Claude Code: gemma3:4b returned an API error for no tool support, qwen2.5-coder:14b printed tool calls as JSON text and took 57s, and Claude Code's tool definitions alone use about 11,000 tokens of context. The author concluded it was 'not practical at this time'. Treat launch success as setup success, not capability. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-30) — https://dev.classmethod.jp/en/articles/claude-code-ollama-local/ · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI

## Facts and statements

- [statement] `ollama launch` was announced in the Ollama blog on 2026-01-23 with Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex and Droid as supported tools; the blog presents it as setup-and-run with no manual environment variables or config files, and `--config` configures a tool without launching it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-23) — https://ollama.com/blog/launch · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI · also: https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/opencode
- [statement] As of the docs mirror, `ollama launch` supports Claude Code (`ollama launch claude`), Codex (`ollama launch codex`), OpenCode (`ollama launch opencode`) and Copilot CLI (`ollama launch copilot`); the list has grown past the four launch-day tools (Droid, DeepSeek Harness `dsh` and others). Check `ollama launch --help` for the live list. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/claude-code · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI · also: https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/copilot-cli, https://ollama.com/blog/launch
- [statement] Headless use: `ollama launch claude --model <m> --yes -- -p "..."` (same shape for `copilot`). `--yes` skips selectors, pulls the model if missing, and requires `--model`; everything after `--` goes straight to the underlying tool. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/claude-code · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI · also: https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/copilot-cli
- [statement] Claude Code manual setup against local Ollama: export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="" and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434, then `claude --model <model>`. For Ollama's cloud without a local install, set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://ollama.com with ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=$OLLAMA_API_KEY. Hosted WebSearch and advanced tool controls are not fully supported through Ollama's Anthropic compatibility, and Claude settings files can override shell variables (check with /status). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/claude-code · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI
- [statement] Codex via `ollama launch codex` refreshes the model catalog and uses a dedicated Codex profile for the session; `--config` configures without launching and `--restore` removes the Ollama launch profile and generated catalog. In Codex, `/model` switches between installed tool-capable Ollama models without a restart. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/codex · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI
- [statement] Codex manual paths: `codex --oss` (optionally `-m <model>`), or a persistent profile `~/.codex/ollama-launch.config.toml` with model_provider "ollama-launch", base_url http://localhost:11434/v1/ and wire_api = "responses". Codex's own repo made the Responses format the default for the built-in `ollama` provider (#8798), and a third-party guide reports the chat-completions wire API was removed from Codex in February 2026, so `wire_api = "chat"` configs no longer work. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/codex · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI · also: https://forge.lthn.ai/core/core-agent-ide/commit/fe03320791eab0f0bc1faecd1291e0fae6bff89d
- [statement] Codex web-search requests sent through the Ollama profile are executed by Ollama for local and cloud models and need `ollama signin`; disable with `codex --profile ollama-launch -c 'web_search="disabled"'`. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/codex · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI
- [statement] GitHub's official Copilot CLI BYOK docs list Ollama as a supported OpenAI-compatible provider. Env vars: COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL (required), COPILOT_MODEL (required, or --model), COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE (openai default, azure, anthropic), COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY (optional; a local Ollama needs none), COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API, and COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS / MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Models must support tool calling and streaming or the CLI errors. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/use-byok-models · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI · also: https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/copilot-cli
- [statement] Copilot CLI `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true` stops contact with GitHub's servers, but it only gives full network isolation if the provider is also local; a remote COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL still receives prompts and code context. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/use-byok-models · keywords: ollama launch and coding-agent integrations: Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot CLI
